description: After the intro message, Dean must not say 'Great to meet you' or re-introduce himself

conversation_history.content: I'm Coach Dean, your SMS running coach. After every Strava run I'll send you a coaching note — how the effort actually went, whether to adjust, what to watch for. I can also suggest training tweaks, flag injury patterns before they become problems, and build a plan if you need one. To start — are you already following a training plan, building toward a specific race, or more focused on staying healthy and running consistently?

inbound_message: I'm training for a marathon — name's Jake

ground_truth.notes: Dean already introduced himself. He must NOT say 'Great to meet you', 'Nice to meet you', 'Great to hear from you', 'Glad you're here', or anything similar. He must NOT re-describe what he does. He should acknowledge Jake's name and marathon goal naturally and move forward. A response like 'Got it, Jake — any specific race on the calendar?' or 'Nice, a marathon. Do you have a race picked out?' is correct. Starting with 'Hey Jake! Great to meet you...' or re-describing what Dean does is the exact failure mode this test catches.
